{{short description|Annual ranking of corporations}}
{{Italic title|string=Fortune}}
{{use mdy dates|date=October 2023}}
The '''''Fortune'' Global 500''', also known as '''Global 500''', is an annual ranking of the top 500 [[corporation]]s worldwide as measured by [[revenue]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Belanger |first=Lydia |title=Fortune Archives: The year the Fortune 500 went Global |url=https://fortune.com/2025/08/03/fortune-archives-the-year-the-fortune-500-went-global/ |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=Fortune |language=en}}</ref> The list is compiled and published annually by ''[[Fortune (magazine)|Fortune]]'' magazine.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hoover |first=Gary |date=2020-06-25 |title=25 Years of the Fortune 500 Animated Chart |url=https://americanbusinesshistory.org/25-years-of-the-fortune-500-animated-chart/ |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=Business History - The American Business History Center |language=en-US}}</ref> It was first published in 1955.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Terrell |first=Ellen |title=Research Guides: This Month in Business History: First Fortune 500 List Published |url=https://guides.loc.gov/this-month-in-business-history/may/first-fortune500-published |access-date=2026-07-14 |website=guides.loc.gov |language=en}}</ref>

== Methodology ==
Until 1989, Global 500 listed only non–[[United States]] industrial corporations under the title "International 500" while the [[Fortune 500|''Fortune'' 500]] contained and still contains exclusively United States corporations. In 1990, United States companies were added to compile a truly global list of top industrial corporations as ranked by sales. Since 1995, the list has had its current form, listing also top financial corporations and service providers by revenue.

Several inconsistencies exist in ''Fortune''{{'s}} ranking of cities with the most ''Fortune'' 500 headquarters. On June 3, 2011, the ''[[Atlanta Business Chronicle]]'' stated examples of ''Fortune'' including regional headquarters for some cities, excluding regional headquarters for other cities and in some cases excluding headquarters that are physically located inside a city limit.<ref>{{cite web|title=Some cities rankings are overstated|url=http://www.bizjournals.com/atlanta/print-edition/2011/06/03/fortune-500-list-overstates-atlantas.html|author=Maria Saporta|publisher=Atlanta Business Chronicle|access-date=October 28, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130714234502/http://www.bizjournals.com/atlanta/print-edition/2011/06/03/fortune-500-list-overstates-atlantas.html|archive-date=July 14, 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Geographical distribution ==
Since 2001, there has been significant change in the geographical distribution of the companies in the Global 500 rankings. Most of this growth is accounted for by a rapid increase in the number of [[China|Chinese]] Global 500 companies, of which there were 116 by 2026, increasing from only 10 in 2001. The number of [[Europe]]an-based companies declined, from 158 to 123, over the same period, as well as [[Japan]]ese-based companies of which there were about 107 in the ranking in 2000 to now only 40 in 2026.

Among the Global 500, 379 companies (75.8%) are from these six countries.
